CANONICAL_NAME.value: LMDB 0.9.31 -- Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (Howard Chu, Symas / OpenLDAP)

value.lineage: B+tree key-value store with single-writer/multi-reader MVCC and copy-on-write pages: crash consistency WITHOUT a write-ahead log (two meta pages, the last committed root wins). Descends from OpenLDAP's back-mdb work (2011); rival to Berkeley DB and to log-structured stores such as LevelDB.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: crash-consistent concurrent key-value storage without a log

value.built_to: give readers a consistent snapshot while one writer commits, and survive a crash at any instant without replaying a log
value.pressure: concurrent readers and a writer on one file; power loss mid-write; bounded memory via the OS page cache
value.success_means: every reader sees a committed root; after a crash the database opens at the last committed state with no repair step

value.pressure: competing writers/readers, partial failure (crash mid-commit), bounded memory
value.failure_condition: a torn write corrupts the tree, or a reader observes a half-committed page
